# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Edit space this iteration: ONLY the system prompt (`prompt.md`). tools.py is not in the
editable artifact set, so every fix is a KNOWLEDGE-gap prompt edit (grounded in the traces
and the SpreadsheetBench grading mechanism).

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Code overfits the ONE visible sample; fails hidden test cases 2 & 3 | 418-29, 374-9, 160-6, 53161, (52216) | Solution is re-run on 3 spreadsheets of the SAME layout but DIFFERENT data & size; agent hardcodes row counts/ranges/positions from the sample, so it breaks on the other two. Prompt never tells the agent there are multiple graded files. | KNOWLEDGE (hidden-grading fact) | Add missing rule: write general, data-driven code; detect extents at runtime; never hardcode counts/ranges/values from the sample. |
| 2 | Reads only the answer_position range as if it were the input extent | 418-29 (t1), 374-9 | answer_position is the WRITE target, not how much input to read; agent limited its read loop to the answer range (e.g. `range(1,8)` for A1:B7) and missed input rows. | KNOWLEDGE | Add rule distinguishing answer_position (write target) from input extent (read dynamically). |
| 3 | Misreads actual sheet layout / writes to wrong cells | 53161 (t2 wrote rows 23-29 for range starting row 22; misread table orientation), 347-49, 160-6 (t0 local-clear instead of real row-delete) | Agent assumes layout from preview instead of inspecting real coordinates; wrong operation semantics for delete-rows. | KNOWLEDGE | Strengthen "inspect real cells first" + explicit delete-rows-shift semantics for Sheet-Level. |
| — | Underspecified / deep-logic single tasks | 55457 (instruction is blank/nbsp — intent unknowable), 32468 (12-month rolling SUMIFS semantics) | Not a shared, prompt-addressable class. | (skipped) | Better inspection may help marginally; no targeted edit. |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit)
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Add missing rule (menu #4) | prompt.md step 2 | States the graded-on-multiple-files fact + "detect at runtime, never hardcode counts/ranges/values from the sample". General across all tasks. | YES — 47484 already fully dynamic; 40467 writes to the given answer_position (unchanged). |
| 2 | Add missing rule / clarify contract | prompt.md step 3 | answer_position = write target, not read extent; read input dynamically. | YES — passing tasks already read full input. |
| 3 | Rewrite for clarity + WHY (menu #1/#2) | prompt.md step 1 & 3 | Inspect real coordinates before computing (preview hides layout); use `data_only=True` for formula cells; real delete_rows shift semantics for Sheet-Level. | YES — passing tasks already inspect/behave this way. |
| 4 | Keep + add WHY (menu #2), do NOT harden | prompt.md step 4 | Kept "prefer literal values" and added the reason (grader recalculates formulas on open). Deliberately did NOT forbid formulas — 40467 passes 3/3 by writing a formula, so a "never formulas" rule would regress it. | YES — matches both passing tasks. |
| 5 | Add missing rule (menu #4) | prompt.md step 5 | Preserve untouched sheets/cells; prefer in-place openpyxl edit over DataFrame rebuild. Soft preference; does not flip a correct output. | YES — 47484 (rebuild) / 418-29-t0 (rebuild) still produce correct output. |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change)
- Cluster 1, trace 418-29 t1 (reward 0.33) hardcoded `range(1,8)` reading only A1:B7 → new step 2 forbids hardcoding the row count and step 3 says read input dynamically; the passing sibling t0 (reward 1.0) already reads the full sheet with pandas → matches the rule, behavior unchanged.
- Cluster 1, trace 374-9 t1 (reward 0.33) hardcoded `range(7,23)` though instruction says "number of rows/columns can vary" → step 2 directs dynamic detection of the used rows/columns.
- Cluster 3, trace 53161 t2 (reward 0.0) misread table orientation & wrote rows 23-29 vs answer starting row 22 → step 1 (inspect real coordinates) + step 3 (write into exactly answer_position). Passing t0 (reward 1.0) already parsed real coordinates → unchanged.
- Cluster 3, trace 160-6 t0 (reward 0.0) cleared-and-rewrote inside range (rows below not shifted) → step 3 mandates real delete_rows shift. Passing t1 (reward 1.0) already used `delete_rows` → unchanged.
- SAFE / non-regression: passing 47484 (dynamic pandas groupby, literals) and 40467 (openpyxl in-place, writes a correct formula to fixed answer_position D1:D10) both already satisfy every new rule; no rule forces a different action or a different graded output for them. Verified 40467 writes a formula and still scores 1.0 across all 5 trials → confirmed the grader recalculates formulas, so step 4 keeps formulas allowed.

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees: serial (single-artifact prompt edit; diagnosis done by scripting over ./trajectories/ JSON — extracting per-trial reward, final code, and the pass/fail A-B within each flaky task, which was faster and more precise than fan-out for a 10-task set).
- Prior iterations read: none exist — LEDGER shows baseline only; ./prior_iterations/ empty. This is the first optimization iteration.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- Do NOT add a "never write formulas / always write literals" rule — 40467 passes by writing a formula; the grader recalculates. Hardening this regresses it.
- The generalization rule (graded on multiple same-structure files → dynamic code) is the highest-leverage lever for this benchmark; keep it prominent.
- answer_position = write target, not read extent.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- 55457: instruction field is empty (a lone nbsp) — the intended transformation is unknowable from a general rule; no safe prompt edit special-cases it without hardcoding.
- 32468: deep, task-specific rolling-12-month SUMIFS semantics; not a shared class a general prompt rule fixes without overfitting. Better inspection (step 1) may help marginally but no targeted edit made.
- Did NOT touch tools.py — it is outside the editable artifact set this iteration.
